subject: shower loofah
title: What If You Never Replaced Your Loofah?

scenes.text: What if you never replaced your loofah? Even a brand new one changes after the first shower.
In a 1994 study, new loofahs started almost clean. Once wet, they filled with a different crowd of bacteria.
Every scrub leaves dead skin in the fibres. That's food, so the bacteria grow even faster.
It never fully dries in a steamy shower. A dermatologist calls it a beautiful breeding ground.
The study began with one person's skin infection traced back to a loofah. Scrub over a cut and that's the risk.
So natural loofahs should go every three or four weeks. Plastic ones, about two months.

What if you never replaced your loofah? A 1994 Journal of Clinical Microbiology study found loofahs, even new ones, quickly fill with bacteria once wet, and trapped skin cells feed them; the study started from a skin infection traced to a loofah.
A Cleveland Clinic dermatologist advises replacing natural loofahs every three to four weeks and plastic ones about every two months.
